title: Choosing MCP's Shape for the Job

questions.question: Which factor most directly decides whether a capability should be exposed as a tool, a resource, or a prompt?
options: Whether the transport is stdio or Streamable HTTP, a detail the primitive never depends on
Who is meant to control it: the model, the application, or the user decide separately
How many bytes the response contains, a size limit no part of the protocol sets
Which language the server is written in, since MCP treats every runtime the same way
questions.explanation: MCP assigns control of each primitive to a specific party: a tool is model controlled, a resource is application driven, and a prompt is user controlled, and that split is what a use case's initiator should decide.

questions.question: A workflow automation use case kicks off a deploy pipeline that can run for twenty minutes before it finishes. Which result shape fits a request that long?
options: A normal complete result, because MCP places no ceiling on how long one response may take
A resource read that streams the growing output back as one ever-expanding text block
A CreateTaskResult from the tasks extension, returning a taskId the client polls to finish
An input_required result, because the client must supply an argument before anything can run
questions.explanation: Work that risks a transport timeout is a good fit for the tasks extension, which returns a durable taskId and status instead of holding the connection open for the full duration.

questions.question: A nightly CI job calls an MCP server with no human present to approve anything. Which authorization path fits that caller?
options: The interactive OAuth 2.1 code flow with PKCE, the same path a person would use
Dynamic Client Registration, completed once by a person before the nightly job ever runs
Credentials read from the environment, since every authorization path assumes a local stdio transport
The OAuth client credentials extension, which authenticates the machine caller with no user present
questions.explanation: The OAuth client credentials authorization extension exists for exactly this case: an unattended, machine-to-machine caller that has no user available to complete an interactive redirect.

questions.question: An internal ticket search tool's tools/list result is only meaningful within one authenticated organization. What must the result carry, and what does that setting not do?
options: cacheScope private, which limits sharing across contexts but is not an access control itself
cacheScope private, which the server also uses as its access control for this list
No cache fields, because the result stays scoped to the session opened earlier on
cacheScope public, because only server/discover results ever carry any caching hints at all
questions.explanation: tools/list is one of the six cacheable operations and must carry cacheScope; private only limits sharing across authorization contexts, it does not itself enforce access control, and 2026-07-28 has no session to scope anything by.

questions.question: A function formats a currency string entirely inside one application process, with no external system, no separate host, and no second consumer. What does this scenario call for?
options: An MCP resource, so the application can read the formatted string as added context
A direct function call, since no external system or second consumer needs a protocol boundary
An MCP tool, so the model can invoke the formatter whenever a number appears
An MCP prompt, so the user can pick a formatting template from a menu
questions.explanation: MCP's value comes from interoperability across hosts and servers; a capability with no second consumer and no separate system to standardize access to gains nothing from a protocol boundary.

questions.question: A usage-dashboard tool ships an MCP Apps UI resource. A client that never declared the io.modelcontextprotocol/ui extension calls it. What should a well-behaved server do?
options: Reject the call outright, because a server treats every extension it offers as mandatory
Return the same interactive iframe, regardless of which capabilities the client happened to declare
Return a normal result with meaningful text, the fallback path for a client lacking it
Add the extension to the client's declared capabilities automatically so the call can proceed
questions.explanation: Extensions are disabled by default and never assumed: a server offering a UI-enhanced tool should still return meaningful text content for a client that has not declared support for it.
